title: Reflective proxy for tenant-aware shadowing and budgeted duplication
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight reflective proxy layer that safely mirrors a bounded subset of production requests to shadow model variants. The proxy must support tenant-level budgets, adaptive sampling, strong isolation (no PII or customer data leakage to shadow backends), and comprehensive telemetry for traffic duplication. This will enable shadow experiments, A/B evaluations, and canary validations without risking runaway costs or cross-tenant interference.
background: We have frequent requests from product and research teams to run shadow experiments against new model checkpoints and quantized variants. Existing duplication flows are ad-hoc and either too expensive (full duplication) or too risky (no tenant quotas and limited observability). Recent incidents showed an unbounded shadow pipeline caused budget spikes for a small number of high-traffic tenants. We need a structured, tenant-aware approach that enforces cost controls and safety constraints.
goals: 1) Provide a reusable reflective proxy that can mirror requests to one or more shadow endpoints with per-tenant quotas and global budget caps. 2) Implement adaptive sampling strategies (probabilistic, stratified by request size and model latency) that can be configured per experiment. 3) Guarantee data isolation and redaction rules before sending to shadow backends. 4) Emit detailed metrics and traces to the Console for cost, success/failure, and fidelity comparisons.
non_goals: 1) Not responsible for building model comparison UIs (that is Console work). 2) Not changing core model runtime execution paths. 3) Not implementing automated model rollback — this ticket focuses on safe mirroring and observability only.
proposed_solution:
Introduce a 'reflective proxy' service that sits at the edge of the gateway routing layer. Key capabilities: 
- Tenant-aware duplication policy: per-tenant daily/weekly token budgets and per-experiment budgets. 
- Sampling engine: supports fixed-rate, top-k request sampling, and stratified sampling based on request size and latency buckets. 
- Redaction/transformation hooks: pluggable pipeline to remove or mask sensitive fields (PII) using a deterministic rule set before duplication. 
- Cost accounting: attribute duplicated tokens to tenant and experiment, integrate with billing estimates in Console. 
- Failure isolation: any shadow errors must be backpressure-isolated and never impact primary request latency or success. 
- Config store: experiment configs stored in ConfigDB with audit logs and rollout history.
Implementation notes: lightweight proxy in Go, using async duplication with durable queue (Kafka or internal queue) and worker pools for mirror dispatches. Request flow must acknowledge primary path immediately and fan-out duplication asynchronously.
acceptance_criteria: Reflective proxy can mirror >= 10K requests/minute of mixed-size requests without affecting primary path p50 latency by more than 2%
Per-tenant budget enforcement prevents duplication beyond set token limits and emits budget-exhausted events to Console
Adaptive sampling modes can be toggled per-experiment via ConfigDB and take effect within 2 minutes
Redaction hooks remove PII fields defined in the policy before any shadow request is sent
Duplication failures do not increase error rates on the primary path and are visible in the tracing dashboard
success_metrics:
- Percentage of experiments using reflective proxy vs ad-hoc mirroring (target 80% within 12 weeks).
- Mean cost per duplicated token decreased by 30% versus naive full-duplication baseline.
- Zero customer incidents caused by mirrored traffic in first 3 months.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): enable only for internal tenants and test experiments with hard budget caps and aggressive sampling (Mar 1 - Mar 15). Phase 2 (beta): open to trusted external tenants, add Console toggle and budget UI, monitor for two weeks. Phase 3 (GA): enable as primary mirroring mechanism and deprecate older duplication flows.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Metrics: duplicated_tokens.total, duplicated_tokens.per_tenant, duplication_failures.rate, budget_exhausted.count, sampling_rate.overrides.
- Traces: distributed trace with fanned-out child spans for each mirrored call.
- Alerts: page on duplication_failures.rate > 1% for 5m or budget_exhausted.count spikes by > 50% over baseline.
- Dashboards: per-experiment fidelity panel showing primary vs shadow response distributions and token split.
cost_controls:
- Global daily duplication cap configurable by org.
- Per-tenant daily/weekly token limits with soft and hard thresholds.
- Experiment-level caps and time windows; auto-disable when limits reached.
- Optional monetary budget enforcement (estimated tokens * unit_price) for large tenants.
- Sampling strategies tuned to favor short requests or higher-information requests to reduce token footprint.
isolation_mechanisms:
- Mandatory redaction pipeline before dispatch to any shadow endpoint.
- No customer identifiers are sent unless experiment explicitly permits and tenant consents.
- Shadow requests run on separate networking and credentials, managed via dedicated service accounts and KMS-wrapped keys.
- Rate-limit shadow dispatch per tenant to avoid downstream saturation.
tasks: Design API contract and config schema for reflective proxy (ConfigDB entries, experiment model)
Implement Go proxy with asynchronous fan-out and durable queue integration
Build sampling engine with fixed-rate and stratified sampling implementations
Create redaction/transformation hook framework and default PII policy
Integrate cost accounting events into Console metrics pipeline
Add tracing hooks and unit/end-to-end tests for failure isolation
Create e2e test harness for tenant budget exhaustion scenarios
Document operator runbook and experiment configuration guide
risks:
- Misconfigured redaction rules could leak sensitive data; require security review and CI checks.
- Budget enforcement bugs could either over-throttle legitimate experiments or allow runaway costs.
- Async duplication introduces eventual consistency in telemetry; need clear semantics in Console.
- Dependence on message queue availability could delay duplication; ensure backpressure and local buffering with safe defaults.
mitigations:
- Mandatory security review and test vectors for PII redaction.
- Canary feature gates and tight defaults (very low sampling) for initial rollout.
- Exhaustive unit tests for budget logic and chaos testing for queue failures.
- Fallback: if queue is down, disable duplication and emit a high-severity telemetry event.
notes: We should coordinate with Billing to ensure any cost attribution is compatible with existing invoicing. Consider adding a user-visible 'shadow cost' line-item in tenant dashboards. Also evaluate whether existing traffic-mirroring libraries can be reused or if building in-house is preferable due to redaction and tenant-scope requirements.
